subject: Follow-up: inference availability interruption — customer dossier, timeline & corrective commitments
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@midcitypay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: inference availability interruption — customer dossier, timeline & corrective commitments

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for your time yesterday. Per our commitment, attached is a concise customer-facing dossier that covers: a clear timeline of the disruption your team saw, root-cause summary at a customer level, immediate mitigations we applied, and our near-term corrective commitments.

TL;DR summary
- What happened: a scheduling bug in the cross-tenant batching controller caused request misrouting under a rare sequence length distribution spike, which led to increased queueing and token-level latency for a subset of routes.
- Impact window: ~2028-02-09 22:03 UTC — 2028-02-10 01:47 UTC for affected requests to the eu-west-1 model pool (you saw >95th percentile token latency and increased timeouts).
- Customer impact: your production inference requests that use the "midcity-prod-v2" route experienced increased tail latency and several 504s; estimated affected request volume = ~0.6% of hourly traffic at peak.

What we are delivering with this email (attachments + actions)
1) A one-page customer dossier (attached) with a plain-English RCA and timeline.
2) A CSV export of the event timeline and request samples (attached) so your engineers can reconcile logs.
3) Our corrective commitments and owners:
   - Fix batching controller scheduling rule and deploy validated patch (owner: Dylan Brooks) — ETA: 48 hours for staged rollout, full rollout 5 business days.
   - Add a route-level circuit-breaker and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant to prevent token-level timeouts (owner: Hannah Schmitt) — ETA: configuration staged in 72 hours, verification in 7 business days.
   - Post-incident observability package for your team: token-level traces, per-route heatmaps, and a replayable request sample (owner: Marissa Cole) — ETA: 3 business days.

Attachments: midcity_incident_timeline.csv (timeline + samples), mitigation_playbook.pdf (customer dossier with mitigation steps and testing results).

Next steps
- Please confirm receipt and whether you'd like a brief walkthrough call; otherwise we will proceed with the timelines above and share verification artifacts as each step completes.
- We will notify you via this thread as each milestone (staged rollout, verification, full rollout) completes.

Apologies again for the disruption — we understand the customer impact and are treating this with top priority.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mitigation_playbook.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: midcity_incident_timeline.csv (CSV)]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@midcitypay.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
Cc: MidCity Pay Ops <ops@midcitypay.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference availability interruption — customer dossier, timeline & corrective commitments

Chloe —

Thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions from Ops: 

1) You mention the impact window ended at 01:47 UTC; can you confirm whether any requests after that time were reprocessed or retried by Redwood, or did MidCity Pay need to requeue client-side?
2) For the proposed circuit-breaker fallback, will the model variant used in fallback change prompt semantics (we rely on a tuned v2 variant for subtle policy prompts)? If so, can you guarantee deterministic fallback behavior and provide a short test plan we can run?
3) Please confirm the ETA for the staged rollout for the scheduling patch and whether there's a canary we can observe (request IDs or dashboard link).

We'd appreciate a short 20-minute sync tomorrow if possible — Ops wants to align on the verification steps before you push the staged rollout.

Regards,
Liam
Head of Platform Engineering
MidCity Pay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference availability interruption — customer dossier, timeline & corrective commitments

Chloe / team —

Quick internal note to confirm we accept the Ops clarifying checks and to capture owners/timing here (copying Dylan for the patch work):

- Dylan: prioritize the scheduling controller patch. Scope for the first staged rollout = eu-west-1 model pool only; provide request IDs for ~100 synthetic requests we can use to observe latency before/after. Please prepare a canary dashboard link (JIRA-9876 will track).
- Hannah: for the circuit-breaker fallback, plan the fallback variant to preserve prompt semantics; if exact parity isn't possible, include a deterministic degradation policy and clearly documented prompt differences. Provide a short test plan (3 test cases) we can run with MidCity Pay.
- Marissa (me): I'll assemble the observability bundle and coordinate a 20-minute sync tomorrow with Liam and Ops (suggested slots: 09:00 or 11:00 PST). I'll own sharing verification artifacts.

Chloe — feel free to confirm the sync time and call attendees with the customer. I'll also add the timeline CSV and dossier to the shared drive link and hand off the JIRA ticket.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@midcitypay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference availability interruption — customer dossier, timeline & corrective commitments

Liam —

Appreciate the quick questions. We can do a 20-minute sync tomorrow at 09:00 PST; I've booked a placeholder and sent a calendar invite to your ops alias. Confirmed answers to your bullets below: 

1) Reprocessing / retries: Redwood did not requeue or reprocess customer-originated requests after 01:47 UTC; failures returned 504s to callers. We have exported the affected request IDs in midcity_incident_timeline.csv so you can reconcile.
2) Fallback semantics: the fallback will target a compatible v2-compat variant and is designed to preserve prompt semantics for the three test cases we'll share. If minor difference exists we will surface exact deltas in the test plan; fallback behavior will be deterministic per-grouping key so you can reason about which requests fall back.
3) Staged rollout ETA for scheduling patch: staged deployment begins 48 hours from initial deploy approval (we plan to start the staged rollout 2028-02-12 09:00 UTC). Canary request IDs and a short dashboard link (JIRA-9876) will be posted prior to rollout start.

Attachments and links: I've placed the dossier and timeline in the shared drive folder and attached copies to this thread.

We will notify you at each milestone and post verification results to the shared drive. If anything changes, we will escalate here immediately.

Best regards,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: midcity_incident_timeline.csv (CSV)]
